name: Ring Row
description: The ring row is a bodyweight horizontal pulling exercise performed with gymnastic rings suspended at an adjustable height. By walking the feet forward or backward, the difficulty scales dramatically — nearly vertical for beginners, nearly horizontal for advanced trainees. The rings' instability demands significant rotator cuff and scapular stabilizer engagement throughout the pull.

execution.starting_position: Hang rings at approximately waist to chest height. Grasp a ring in each hand and walk feet forward under the rings until the body is at an angle — the more horizontal the body, the harder the exercise. Arms are extended with the body forming a straight line from head to heels.
execution.setup_instructions: Secure rings overhead from a pull-up bar, beam, or dedicated rack. Set height based on difficulty level — higher rings create an easier angle. Keep feet flat on the floor or elevated on a box to increase difficulty.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms extended, body in a straight plank position, rings at arm's length.
Step 2: Keeping the body rigid, retract the scapulae and row the chest up toward the rings.
Step 3: As you pull, allow the rings to rotate outward naturally and squeeze the chest to the rings.
Step 4: At the top, the rings should be at chest level and the elbows behind the torso.
Step 5: Slowly extend the arms and lower back to the starting position, maintaining body rigidity.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you row up. Inhale as you lower.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag — the entire body must stay rigid as a plank
Pulling the rings to the neck rather than the chest
Not completing full arm extension at the bottom
safety_considerations: Verify ring straps and anchor point are rated for your body weight before beginning
Increase angle gradually — do not attempt a fully horizontal position without sufficient pulling strength
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at the bottom to rings touching the chest at the top.
coaching_cues: Your body is a rigid board — nothing bends except the elbows and shoulders
Think 'chest to rings' not 'chin to rings'
Rotate the pinkies up as you pull to maximize rear delt and rhomboid contraction
